summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with recurrent abdominal pain centered at the G-tube site and epigastric region, worsening after a recent G-tube exchange in clinic. Initial evaluation revealed no infection, obstruction, or perforation on imaging. CT showed ill-defined inflammatory changes around the G-tube insertion site without abscess. Pain was managed with oxycodone, and tube feeds were continued to prevent hypoglycemia. The patient developed asymptomatic hypotension, likely due to atenolol and pain-related hypovolemia, prompting discontinuation of atenolol to avoid masking hypoglycemia symptoms. Pain improved during the stay, and the patient was discharged home with a two-week supply of oxycodone, instructions to follow up with pain management and GI for EGD, and advised to discontinue atenolol permanently.
problems: Chronic gastrojejunal ulcer without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
